title: Randomized time is contained in nondeterministic time
statement: For every function $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{RTIME}(T) \subseteq \mathrm{NTIME}(T)$. The randomized class requires a finite machine running in time bounded by a constant multiple of $T$, halting on every branch, accepting members with probability at least $2/3$, and never accepting nonmembers; the nondeterministic class requires a finite machine with that time bound, halting on every branch and accepting exactly the members.
